craft_notes: Sthāyin: vīra of the sealed proof — utsāha as each consequence collapses and the maker stands. Rebirth-vs-no-meeting contradiction; vain close. Rejected: (a) vain→false → killed: vain is aired. Read aloud: ONCE-need IS-gone … THE-claim IS-vain.

lines: Once need is gone, no meeting with the soul again;
yet minds are born in bodies still — the claim is vain.
l4.sanskrit_cite: arthitvavigamān na syād bhūyaḥ puṃsā samāgamaḥ

reads_against.argmap: No reunion — and yet born? → Liberation-by-needlessness contradicts rebirth.
c1_essence: The svabhāva-view's consequences pressed: desired-by-all yet body-changes by nature; occurrence without union; needlessness fitting neither spirit nor mind; no reunion yet rebirth; mokṣa collapsed into nature; compassion-acts forcing passion-exhaustion doctrine (vv46-51).
The siddhānta sealed: nature-view abandoned as unjust, bodies famously sentient-maker-prior, arrangement-difference the flawless proof, the hetu aimed at Parameśvara unshaken (vv52-54).
